purpose: Records the relock of the OpenHands recipe lock (blueprints/runtime-workers/openhands/requirements.lock) from litellm 1.93.0 to 1.93.2. OSV published GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222 (CVE-2026-84377, 'LiteLLM: Authenticated SSRF and provider-credential exfiltration via unvalidated request-body routing parameters', GitHub severity Moderate, CVSS 3.1 6.5, CWE-918) at 2026-09-30T21:11:25Z for litellm 1.93.0 and 1.93.1; 1.93.2 is the first release of the 1.93 line without it. The required osv-scanner check has failed on the lock for every head since 22:10Z, main's own push runs included, so no pull request could merge. The change replaces the litellm requirement line and its hashes and nothing else in the lock, rebinds the lock's IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS entry in tests/test_osv_lockfile_coverage.py to the relocked sha256 and to this record (the 2026-09-29 oauthlib review is carried forward at the new digest, not rerun), and adds no ignore.
authorization: The lock's owner session (bc, native-agent-stack-bc) is gone: a peer listing on 2026-09-30 no longer shows it. The merge-train owner (session sota-default-harness-setup) asked the Gate A owner (session native-agent-stack-6d, this record's author) to take the relock and to relock rather than ignore. Peer messages are not retained evidence; the reproductions in sections B, D and F of the returned outputs are. No user decision is needed: the change follows the recipe's own method (research.md 'Runtime lock security relock') and adds no exception.
evidence_class: Local runs on this host of the pinned OSV-Scanner 2.6.0 with the repository's config and the workflow's own lockfile lists, a local reproduction of the relock with uv 0.12.17 from the pinned upstream source archive, the recipe's own install sequence in a scratch venv on the host network (no model request: not the image and not an OpenHands run), reads of registry and advisory records (OSV API, PyPI JSON API), a blobless depth-1 fetch of two upstream git tags (BerriAI/litellm v1.93.0 and v1.93.2), and one CI job log (gh run view --job). Static and local: the diffs, hash equalities and text searches are structural checks, not executions. Returned outputs: blueprints/runtime-workers/openhands/evidence/relock-2026-09-30-litellm.txt.
limitations: The relock covers only the recipe venv. The agent-server image's server is a PyInstaller build of upstream's unchanged uv.lock, which still pins litellm 1.93.0 (section C: the archive's root uv.lock, line 2175), and the 2026-09-28 grype record of that image predates the advisory and was not rerun. Whether the advisory reaches the image's binary is unmeasured. The grader venv (OpenHands/benchmarks@405bae7's uv.lock, digest in pins.json grader.uv_lock_sha256) is outside this lock and outside .github/osv-scanner-lockfiles.json; its litellm version was not read.

The advisory concerns the LiteLLM proxy: an authenticated proxy user routing a provider call with request-body parameters the proxy did not validate. The recipe runs no LiteLLM proxy, and no installed package outside litellm imports litellm.proxy (section H: 0 files). That is a static text search of the installed .py files of the relocked venv, not a runtime trace; a name assembled at run time would not match. It is context only: the change moves to the fixed release and the decision does not rest on reachability.

No OpenHands task ran with the relocked venv. The install check ran the recipe's install sequence, uv pip check and the SDK import check on the host network (no model request); the image installation, model behavior and any runtime path through litellm 1.93.2 are unmeasured. An installation that recorded the old requirements_sha256 must re-run install (host.py:1432-1433 refuses with matching_successful_installation_required); whether this host holds such a record was not checked for this change.

litellm 1.93.2 differs from 1.93.0 in 34 files of upstream source (section C): proxy auth, health, SSO and server modules, two library files outside the proxy (litellm/caching/dual_cache.py: the in-memory TTL of a value read back from Redis; litellm/litellm_core_utils/url_utils.py: one new helper function), two provider modules (huggingface embedding, oobabooga), the non-root Dockerfile, pyproject.toml, uv.lock and tests. None is under the paths the recipe cites or calls (litellm/llms/openai, litellm/responses, litellm/main.py, litellm/router.py, litellm/types, litellm/utils.py). The comparison is of upstream source at the two tags; the installed wheels were verified against the lock's hashes only and were not diffed against those tags.

The upstream workspace cannot produce this lock as published: its pyproject.toml pins litellm==1.93.0 (line 19) and caps litellm at exclude-newer-package 2026-07-20T00:00:00Z (line 8), which excludes 1.93.1 and 1.93.2. The relock edits both lines in a scratch extraction (section B prints the whole diff); the upstream lock, the agent-server image and the SDK's own release are unchanged. The next upstream lock that carries litellm >= 1.93.2 makes the edit unnecessary.

The OSV database is the live API at scan time. The clean result holds for 2026-09-30 only: an advisory published later for any pinned package fails the required check again. Every statement about a release window is as of 2026-09-30T23:04:45Z: litellm 1.93.2's files were uploaded 2026-08-09T02:16:21Z to 02:17:49Z, 52 days earlier.

The ignore reasons of the two oauthlib advisories in .github/osv-scanner.toml still cite evidence/receipts/osv-openhands-pyjwt-relock-20260930.json for the OpenHands lock 'at its relocked sha256'; that text already lagged the 2026-09-30 urllib3 relock and is unchanged here (PR #535 edits the same file). The binding record is the IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS entry of tests/test_osv_lockfile_coverage.py, which this change rebinds. The dated paragraph that each earlier relock added to docs/decisions/2026-09-22-github-automation-closure.md is also not added here: PR #555 edits that file, so the paragraph follows its merge.

Open pull requests that add locks to the scan inventory (#535 and #551 change .github/osv-scanner-lockfiles.json) were not read for their litellm pins; any lock in the inventory that pins litellm 1.93.0 or 1.93.1 fails the same check.

release_choice.selected: litellm 1.93.2: the first release of the 1.93 line that OSV lists without the advisory (1.93.0 and 1.93.1 are affected), the line upstream's workspace pins (litellm==1.93.0) and inside the SDK's own constraint (openhands-sdk/pyproject.toml: litellm>=1.93.0); uploaded 2026-08-09, outside every cooldown

alternatives.why_not: a fixed release exists and is outside the 7-day window; OSV-Scanner 2.6.0 matches an ignore by id in every lock of an invocation (the header of IGNORE_SCOPES in tests/test_osv_lockfile_coverage.py), so an ignore is repo-wide, and it would need a reachability review of an advisory the relock makes moot

alternatives.option: a newer line (1.94.3, 1.95.1 or 1.96.2, each named as fixed in the advisory record)
alternatives.why_not: a larger jump than the fix needs, away from the line upstream's workspace pins; their release dates and compatibility were not read

alternatives.option: wait for upstream's workspace to move

release_choice.overturn: (a) OSV lists an advisory for litellm 1.93.2 that only a later release fixes; (b) an OpenHands run of the recipe fails with litellm 1.93.2 and passes with 1.93.0; (c) upstream's workspace publishes a lock with litellm >= 1.93.2: the next relock follows that lock instead of the two-line edit.
